questions.question: Q1. Define capacitance and find that of a parallel-plate capacitor.
questions.answer: Capacitance C = Q/V (charge per unit potential difference), unit farad (F). A parallel-plate capacitor has C = ε₀A/d (in vacuum), increasing with plate area A and decreasing with separation d.
questions.example: Doubling A doubles C; doubling d halves C.

questions.question: Q2. Find C for a 0.1 m², 1 mm plate capacitor in air.
Q3. State the equivalent capacitance for capacitors in series and in parallel.
questions.answer: Series: 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + … (all same charge). Parallel: C_eq = C₁ + C₂ + … (all same voltage).
questions.shortcut: Series: add reciprocals; Parallel: add directly.
questions.example: Two 4 μF in series → 2 μF; in parallel → 8 μF.

questions.question: Q4. Two capacitors 3 μF and 6 μF are in series. Find C_eq and the voltage across each if 9 V is applied.
questions.answer: C_eq = (3×6)/(3+6) = 18/9 = 2 μF. Charge Q = C_eq V = 2×9 = 18 μC. Across 3 μF: V=18/3=6 V; across 6 μF: V=18/6=3 V (smaller C, larger V).
questions.shortcut: Series Q same; C_eq = product/sum; V ∝ 1/C.
questions.example: 3 μF gets 6 V, 6 μF gets 3 V.

questions.question: Q5. Explain the effect of inserting a dielectric slab.
questions.answer: A dielectric polarizes (bound charges appear), reducing the field and increasing the capacitance by the relative permittivity K: C_new = K C_air. It also lowers the breakdown field and the energy stored for a given voltage.
questions.shortcut: C_new = K C_air ; dielectric reduces the field.

questions.question: Q6. Define polarization and displacement field.
questions.answer: Polarization P is the dipole moment per unit volume of a dielectric (P = N p). The electric displacement D = ε₀E + P; for a linear dielectric D = εE, and the free charge is related by ∇·D = ρ_free. ▥ 22.1–22.3 Capacitance, Parallel Plate & Combinations  —  Compare / Contrast Tables Capacitance: What Determines C Series vs Parallel Capacitor Combinations ▣ 22.4 Energy of a Charged Capacitor
questions.shortcut: P = dipole/volume ; D = εE ; D depends on free charge.
questions.example: A ferroelectric has a large P.

questions.question: Q7. Find the energy stored in a capacitor and show U = ½CV².
questions.answer: Charging, each bit dq needs Vdq of work; integrating gives U = ½CV² = Q²/2C. The energy resides in the electric field between the plates.
questions.example: A 2 μF at 10 V stores ½×2×10⁻⁶×100 = 100 μJ.

questions.question: Q8. Find the energy density in the field of a parallel-plate capacitor.
questions.answer: Total energy U = ½CV²; volume = A d. Energy density u = U/(Ad) = ½ε₀E² (for air, E = V/d). Energy is stored in the field.
questions.example: Higher E → more stored energy density.

questions.question: Q9. Two capacitors (1 and 2 F) are charged to 10 V in parallel then discharged through a resistor. Find total energy dissipated.
questions.answer: Energy in each: ½(1)(100)=50 J and ½(2)(100)=100 J; total = 150 J, which is dissipated as heat in the resistor.
questions.shortcut: U = ½CV² summed; heat = total stored.

questions.question: Q10. Explain energy storage in a capacitor battery (capsule).
questions.answer: A capacitor battery stores charge separated on conductors (plates), holding energy in the electric field; the equivalent capacitance of the battery determines how much charge it can hold at a given voltage, and the stored energy is ½CV². ▥ 22.4 Energy of a Charged Capacitor  —  Compare / Contrast Tables Energy in a Capacitor: Three Equivalent Forms ▣ 22.5 Dielectrics & Polarization (extra)
questions.example: A 1000 F supercap battery at 5 V stores ~12 500 J.

questions.question: Q11. Differentiate free charge and bound charge in a dielectric.
questions.answer: Free charge is mobile charge (e.g. on a plate); bound charge is the polarization charge (P·n) that appears at dielectric surfaces and is not freely mobile. The two cancel inside a bulk dielectric.
questions.shortcut: Free = plates; Bound = surface of the dielectric.
questions.example: The bound surface charge reduces the field inside.

questions.question: Q12. Explain displacement (D) and why it is useful for capacitors.
questions.answer: D = ε₀E + P is the electric displacement field; in a linear dielectric D = εE. D depends only on free charge, which is convenient for capacitor problems where one wants to use the free (not the bound) charge in Gauss's law.
questions.example: Using D one can apply Gauss's law with only free charge.

questions.question: Q13. How does a dielectric increase a capacitor's breakdown voltage?
questions.answer: A good dielectric has a high dielectric strength (resistance to breakdown) and traps charge, so the capacitor can be charged to a higher voltage before the insulating medium breaks down. This lets one store more energy in a given volume. ▥ 22.5 Dielectrics & Polarization (extra)  —  Compare / Contrast Tables Conductor vs Dielectric (in a field) PROFESSOR'S THEORY & VIVA BANK   — the kinds of theory a professor / examiner actually asks
questions.shortcut: High K + high dielectric strength → higher V_breakdown.
questions.example: Ceramic caps use dielectrics for higher voltage.

theoryItems.question: [Derive] T1. Derive the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor.
theoryItems.answer: The field between the plates is E = σ/ε₀ = Q/(ε₀A). The potential difference is V = E·d = Qd/(ε₀A). Hence C = Q/V = ε₀A/d.
theoryItems.shortcut: V = Ed ; E = Q/ε₀A → C = ε₀A/d.
theoryItems.example: Air ~ ε₀; a dielectric replaces ε₀ by ε = ε₀ε_r.

theoryItems.question: [Derive] T2. Derive the energy stored in a charged capacitor (U = ½CV²).
theoryItems.answer: Charging, a small charge dq requires a potential Vdq of work; integrating from 0 to Q gives U = ½QV = ½CV² = Q²/2C. The energy is stored in the electric field between the plates.
theoryItems.example: A 2 μF at 10 V stores 100 μJ.

theoryItems.question: [State] T3. Define capacitance and state the formula for a parallel-plate capacitor.
theoryItems.answer: Capacitance C = Q/V (charge per unit potential difference), in farads (F). A parallel-plate capacitor in vacuum has C = ε₀A/d, increasing with plate area A and decreasing with separation d.
theoryItems.example: Larger plates or closer spacing → bigger C.

theoryItems.question: [Compare] T4. Compare the behaviour of capacitors and resistors in series/parallel.
theoryItems.answer: Resistors in series add directly (R_eq = ΣR); in parallel their reciprocals add. Capacitors do the opposite: in series their reciprocals add (1/C_eq = Σ1/C); in parallel they add directly (C_eq = ΣC). This is the classic exam trap.
theoryItems.shortcut: R: series add; C: parallel add.

theoryItems.question: [Explain] T5. Explain the series and parallel combinations of capacitors.
theoryItems.answer: Series: the same charge is on each and 1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ + … (like resistors in parallel). Parallel: the same voltage and C_eq = C₁ + C₂ + … (like resistors in series).
theoryItems.shortcut: Series: add reciprocals; Parallel: add directly.
theoryItems.example: Two 4 μF: series 2 μF, parallel 8 μF.

theoryItems.question: [Explain] T6. Explain the effect of inserting a dielectric slab into a capacitor.
theoryItems.answer: A dielectric polarizes (bound charges appear at its surfaces), reducing the field for the same free charge; the capacitance rises by the relative permittivity K: C_new = K C_air. The dielectric also raises the breakdown voltage, allowing more energy to be stored in the same volume.

theoryItems.question: [Explain] T7. Explain polarization and the displacement field D.
theoryItems.answer: Polarization P is the dipole moment per unit volume (P = Np). The electric displacement D = ε₀E + P; for a linear dielectric D = εE, and ∇·D = ρ_free. D is useful because it depends only on free charge, not the bound polarization charge.
theoryItems.example: Applying Gauss's law to D uses free charge only.

theoryItems.question: [Explain] T8. Explain a variable capacitor and its use in tuning.
theoryItems.answer: A variable capacitor has rotating plates whose overlap area A changes; C = ε₀A/d varies with the position, so rotating the plates tunes a circuit's resonant frequency. Used in radio and old TVs to select stations.
theoryItems.shortcut: C = ε₀A/d ; rotating plates changes A.
theoryItems.example: Old radios use a variable capacitor to tune.

theoryItems.question: [Explain] T9. Explain the energy density in the electric field of a capacitor.
theoryItems.answer: The total energy U = ½CV²; per unit volume, u = ½ε₀E² (in air). This shows that the energy is stored in the field, not on the plates themselves — a capacitor stores energy in the space between its plates.

theoryItems.question: [Numerical] T10. Two 4 μF capacitors are in series across 20 V. Find the charge on each and the energy of each.
theoryItems.answer: C_eq = 4×4/8 = 2 μF. Q = C_eq V = 2×20 = 40 μC on each (series). Voltage splits: V₁ = Q/C₁ = 10 V, V₂ = 10 V. U₁ = ½CV² = ½×4e-6×100 = 2×10⁻⁴ J each.

Answer:  Capacitance C = Q/V (charge per unit potential difference), unit farad (F). A parallel-plate capacitor has C = ε₀A/d (in vacuum), increasing with plate area A and decreasing with separation d.

Example:  Doubling A doubles C; doubling d halves C.
Q2. Find C for a 0.1 m², 1 mm plate capacitor in air.
⚡ Shortcut:  C = ε₀A/d.
Example:  ≈ 0.89 nF.

⚡ Shortcut:  Series: add reciprocals; Parallel: add directly.
Example:  Two 4 μF in series → 2 μF; in parallel → 8 μF.

Example:  3 μF gets 6 V, 6 μF gets 3 V.

Answer:  A dielectric polarizes (bound charges appear), reducing the field and increasing the capacitance by the relative permittivity K: C_new = K C_air. It also lowers the breakdown field and the energy stored for a given voltage.
⚡ Shortcut:  C_new = K C_air ; dielectric reduces the field.

Answer:  Polarization P is the dipole moment per unit volume of a dielectric (P = N p). The electric displacement D = ε₀E + P; for a linear dielectric D = εE, and the free charge is related by ∇·D = ρ_free.
⚡ Shortcut:  P = dipole/volume ; D = εE ; D depends on free charge.
